claim.pdf_says: The uncaptioned flowchart on page 1188 (printed page 1158) carries three control-flow edges that are drawn, not implied: (a) a line leaves the LEFT edge of the box "Augment identifier-5 with current BY value", runs left and upward, and ends in an arrowhead entering the flow immediately ABOVE the box "Execute specified set of statements"; (b) a line leaves the LEFT edge of the box "Augment identifier-2 with current BY value", runs left and upward the full height of the figure, and ends in an arrowhead entering the flow immediately ABOVE the box "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value"; (c) the "True" exit of "Condition-2" runs to the right, turns down, and rejoins the main flow BELOW "Augment identifier-5 with current BY value" and above "Condition-1". Only the "True" exit of "Condition-1" reaches "Exit".

claim.why_it_matters: The entire purpose of this figure is to show the NESTED loop structure of the VARYING/AFTER phrases of PERFORM with TEST AFTER: the inner loop returns to "Execute specified set of statements" and the outer loop returns to "Set identifier-5 to current FROM value" (re-initialising the inner variable on every outer iteration). With all three edges dropped the markdown reads as a straight-line, single-pass sequence, which is the opposite of what the figure states, and it silently removes the re-initialisation of identifier-5 that distinguishes PERFORM VARYING ... AFTER from two independent loops. The transcription of the neighbouring figures does preserve loop-backs (page 1186 uses fenced box-drawing art, page 1187 draws "↑_________________________________|"), so this page is an outlier, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on both sides, independently, at 300 dpi.

PDF SIDE (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1188/spec_p1188.png, rendered by scripts/spec/page_workunit.py, plus two zoomed crops). All three edges are physically drawn on the page; I traced each one:
(a) A horizontal segment leaves the LEFT edge of "Augment identifier-5 with current BY value", runs left to an inner vertical rail, climbs that rail, and terminates in a solid filled arrowhead that enters the main vertical flow in the gap BETWEEN "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value" and "Execute specified set of statements" -- i.e. the inner loop re-enters at "Execute specified set of statements" WITHOUT re-running "Set identifier-5". Verified in the top crop: the second right-pointing arrowhead sits directly above the "Execute specified set of statements" box.
(b) A horizontal segment leaves the LEFT edge of "Augment identifier-2 with current BY value", runs left to an OUTER vertical rail further left than the inner rail, climbs the full height of the figure, and terminates in a solid filled arrowhead entering the main flow in the gap BETWEEN "Set identifier-2 to cur-rent FROM value" and "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value" -- i.e. the outer loop re-enters at "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value", which is exactly the AFTER-phrase re-initialisation. Verified in the top crop as the first (upper, leftmost-sourced) right-pointing arrowhead.
(c) The "True" exit of "Condition-2" runs right, turns down a right-hand vertical rail, turns left at a point BELOW the bottom of the "Augment identifier-5 with current BY value" box, and merges into the main vertical flow immediately above the down-arrow into "Condition-1". Verified in the bottom crop: the right rail's elbow and the merge into the arrow feeding "Condition-1" are unambiguous.
Only "Condition-1"'s "True" exit carries an arrow to "Exit"; "Condition-2" has no path to "Exit". The page carries no figure caption (footer is "1158  (c)ISO/IEC 2023" and the licence line), so the claim's "uncaptioned" is accurate as well.

MARKDOWN SIDE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, page-1188 block at source line 47982). The quoted markdown is verbatim exact -- I diffed it against the extracted page-1188.md and every line matches, including line order. The block contains ZERO loop-back notation of any kind: no back-arrow, no rail, no "↑...|" run, no box-drawing art. The workunit metadata even records "has_figure": false for this page.

I attempted every listed refutation and none applies:
- Not present-but-reflowed: I searched the whole page block; there is no edge notation anywhere in it, on an adjacent line or otherwise.
- Not adjacent-page spillover: the preceding block (page 1187) ends with the "Figure D.14" caption and the following block (page 1189) opens "## D.27 Example of free-form reference format". Neither carries the missing edges nor any prose restating them.
- Not page-break furniture / wrapping / hyphenation: three whole graph edges are gone, not whitespace.
- Not a misquote: both sides quoted correctly.
- Does change meaning, decisively: the surviving markdown is a valid straight-line reading, so a reader gets a wrong-but-plausible model rather than obviously-broken text.
- The "outlier, not house style" support also checks out: page 1186's block does render loop-backs with fenced box-drawing art ("|◄──...", "└──...►") and page 1187's block does carry "↑_________________________________|".
verdict.corrected_description:
Real, and the claim understates the damage in one respect. All three edges are confirmed drawn in the PDF and all three are absent from the markdown, exactly as described. Two corrections/additions:

(1) The loss of edge (c) is not a mere omission -- it is a corruption. The markdown emits "Condition-2 → True" as a DANGLING arrow with no destination, two lines above the visually parallel "Condition-1 → True → Exit". A reader completes the pattern by analogy and concludes Condition-2's True branch also terminates the PERFORM. The PDF states the opposite: Condition-2 True falls through to the Condition-1 test (the outer-loop test), and ONLY Condition-1 True reaches Exit. So the markdown does not just drop the inner loop; it inverts the meaning of the inner loop's exit.

(2) The precise re-entry targets are worth recording verbatim for anyone repairing the transcription, because they are the whole semantic content of the AFTER phrase: the inner back-edge (from "Augment identifier-5") re-enters ABOVE "Execute specified set of statements" and therefore BELOW "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value", so identifier-5 is NOT re-initialised per inner iteration; the outer back-edge (from "Augment identifier-2") re-enters ABOVE "Set identifier-5 to cur-rent FROM value" and therefore BELOW "Set identifier-2 to cur-rent FROM value", so identifier-5 IS re-initialised on every outer iteration while identifier-2 is initialised once. That asymmetry is the sole difference between PERFORM VARYING ... AFTER and two independent loops, and it is precisely what the flattened transcription destroys.

One incidental observation outside the claim, noted so it is not mistaken for part of this finding: the page-1188 figure is uncaptioned in the PDF itself (verified), while page 1187's one-condition figure carries the caption "Figure D.14 -- ... having two conditions". That caption/figure mismatch is an ISO-side anomaly on pages 1187/1188 and is a separate item from this transcription defect.
